story_title: NVIDIA Ships Vera: Its First Custom CPU Built Specifically for AI Agents
why_this_story: While public attention remains focused on GPU FLOPs, agentic AI has introduced a massive software bottleneck: code execution, tool orchestration, and sandbox management run on CPUs. NVIDIA building and shipping its first custom CPU specifically to unlock AI agents represents a major paradigm shift in AI infrastructure.
viral_angle: NVIDIA dominates GPUs, so why is VP Ian Buck hand-delivering custom CPUs to OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, and SpaceX?
story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI runs purely on GPUs, but agentic AI relies heavily on Python code execution and tool calling—forcing NVIDIA to build its first custom CPU.
story_arc: Hook → Setup → Tension → Reveal → Consequence → Payoff

slides.headline: The hidden bottleneck inside AI agents
slides.body: Traditional chatbots just generated text on a GPU. But AI agents do work: they run Python scripts, compile code, execute tools, and manage long-context retrieval sandboxes. That isn't GPU work—it's CPU work.

slides.headline: GPUs are sitting idle waiting for code to run
slides.body: When an agent solves a complex task, it generates code and waits for execution. Standard server CPUs were never built for thousands of real-time agent sandboxes running simultaneously, causing severe execution bottlenecks.

slides.headline: Meet Vera: NVIDIA's custom CPU for agentic AI

caption:
NVIDIA dominated the AI era with GPUs—now it's building CPUs.

VP Ian Buck has personally delivered the first NVIDIA Vera CPU servers to OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Oracle, and SpaceXAI.

Here is why this matters: AI agents don't just talk. They run Python code, call APIs, manage sandboxes, and perform long-context retrievals. That work doesn't run on GPUs—it requires intensive CPU orchestration.

Without specialized CPU hardware, high-end GPUs sit idle waiting for code execution to finish. Vera is built specifically for this bottleneck, featuring 88 custom Olympus cores and 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Oracle Cloud (OCI) has already committed to deploying hundreds of thousands of Vera chips beginning in 2026.

As AI transitions from answering questions to executing autonomous work, the CPU is making a massive comeback.

What do you think? Will custom AI CPUs replace traditional x86 server chips in data centers?
